subject: medicine
title: Liddle syndrome, polycystic kidney disease, and inherited tubular disorders

steps.tx: Constitutive hyperactivation of collecting duct sodium channels creates a state of monogenic volume-expanded arterial hypertension. Transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait, **Liddle syndrome** results from gain-of-function mutations in the SCNN1B or SCNN1G genes encoding beta or gamma subunits of the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC). These mutations delete the conserved proline-rich PY motif, abolishing binding of the ubiquitin ligase Nedd4-2. Lacking ubiquitination, ENaC channels remain permanently anchored within the apical membrane, driving relentless sodium reabsorption, hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis, and profound suppression of both plasma renin and aldosterone.
steps.say: Constitutive activation of collecting duct sodium channels causes severe inherited hypertension. Transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait, Liddle syndrome results from gain-of-function mutations in the epithelial sodium channel. These mutations prevent channel ubiquitination and degradation, driving relentless sodium reabsorption, hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis, and profound suppression of both plasma renin and aldosterone.

vis.alt: Diagram showing ENaC channel regulation, Nedd4-2 ubiquitin binding, and Liddle syndrome.
vis.caption: Constitutive apical ENaC channel retention and suppressed aldosterone in Liddle syndrome. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Differentiating monogenic hypertensive channelopathies directs specific pharmacological targeting of apical versus nuclear transport mechanisms. Evaluating **pseudo-hyperaldosteronism mechanisms** demonstrates that Liddle syndrome responds exclusively to direct apical ENaC channel blockers such as amiloride or triamterene. Because the defect operates downstream of the mineralocorticoid receptor, competitive aldosterone receptor antagonists like spironolactone or eplerenone are completely ineffective. In contrast, mineralocorticoid excess states like Conn syndrome display elevated circulating aldosterone and exhibit exquisite therapeutic responsiveness to spironolactone.
steps.say: Differentiating inherited hypertensive channelopathies directs pharmacological targeting of specific transport mechanisms. Evaluating pseudo-hyperaldosteronism mechanisms demonstrates that Liddle syndrome responds exclusively to direct ENaC channel blockers like amiloride. Because the molecular defect lies downstream of mineralocorticoid receptors, spironolactone is completely ineffective despite hypokalaemia and hypertension.

left.title: Liddle Syndrome
points: Suppressed plasma renin AND suppressed aldosterone

right.title: Primary Aldosteronism (Conn)
points: Suppressed plasma renin with markedly elevated aldosterone

steps.tx: Failure of collecting duct principal cells to respond to antidiuretic hormone impairs urinary concentration, precipitating massive hypotonic polyuria. Diagnosing **nephrogenic diabetes insipidus** involves genetic or acquired resistance to circulating vasopressin. Ninety percent of hereditary cases involve X-linked recessive mutations in the vasopressin V2 receptor (AVPR2), with the remainder caused by autosomal recessive mutations in the aquaporin-two water channel (AQP2). Acquired causes include chronic lithium therapy, hypercalcaemia, severe hypokalaemia, and demeclocycline. Patients excrete voluminous dilute urine (osmolality under three hundred milliosmoles per kilogram) that fails to concentrate following exogenous desmopressin administration.
steps.say: Failure of collecting duct cells to respond to antidiuretic hormone impairs water reabsorption, causing massive hypotonic polyuria. Diagnosing nephrogenic diabetes insipidus involves genetic or acquired resistance to circulating vasopressin. Most hereditary cases involve X-linked V2 receptor mutations, while acquired causes include lithium toxicity and hypercalcaemia, failing to concentrate urine after desmopressin injection.

rows: Urine osmolality fails to rise (<10% increase)
Urine osmolality fails to rise (<10% increase)
Partial or absent response to dDAVP
Amiloride (blocks lithium entry) or stop lithium
Replacement with oral or intranasal Desmopressin

steps.tx: Progressive development and expansion of fluid-filled cysts derived from renal tubular segments culminate in massive bilateral organ enlargement and functional parenchymal destruction. Transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait, **autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease** (ADPKD) represents the most prevalent monogenic kidney disorder worldwide. Epithelial cell hyperproliferation, abnormal fluid secretion into cyst lumens, and defective primary cilium mechanosensation drive continuous cyst growth. Clinical presentations include early arterial hypertension, recurrent flank pain, macroscopic haematuria from cyst rupture, nephrolithiasis, and progressive decline toward end-stage renal disease by the fifth or sixth decade.
steps.say: Progressive expansion of fluid-filled cysts within renal tubules causes massive bilateral kidney enlargement and parenchymal destruction. Transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait, autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease represents the most common monogenic renal disorder. Abnormal tubular proliferation and cyst fluid secretion drive continuous kidney enlargement, presenting with early hypertension, flank pain, and haematuria.

vis.alt: Ultrasound and macroscopic appearance of massive bilateral cystic kidneys in ADPKD.
vis.caption: Bilateral massive cystic architectural distortion and parenchymal loss in ADPKD. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Genotype-phenotype correlations in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease predict the velocity of cyst expansion and the age of terminal renal failure. Pathological mutations in **PKD1** on chromosome sixteen (encoding the transmembrane mechanosensory protein polycystin-one) account for approximately seventy-eight to eighty-five percent of cases, producing an aggressive clinical course with median progression to end-stage renal disease by age fifty-four to fifty-eight. In contrast, mutations in PKD2 on chromosome four (encoding polycystin-two, a calcium-permeable cation channel) account for fifteen percent of cases, presenting with milder cyst burden and delayed renal failure.
steps.say: Genotype correlations in polycystic kidney disease indicate the speed of cyst expansion and the age of kidney failure. Pathological mutations in PKD1 on chromosome sixteen account for eighty percent of cases, producing aggressive cyst growth with end-stage renal failure around age fifty-five. Mutations in PKD2 cause milder disease, with renal failure delayed until the eighth decade.

left.title: PKD1 Mutation (Chromosome 16p13)
points: Accounts for 78% to 85% of clinical ADPKD
More severe disease with accelerated cyst expansion
Median age of end-stage renal disease: 54 to 58 years

right.title: PKD2 Mutation (Chromosome 4q21)
points: Milder clinical phenotype with slower nephron loss
Median age of end-stage renal disease: 74 years

steps.tx: Systemic expression of polycystin proteins in vascular smooth muscle and non-renal epithelia produces serious extrarenal complications in polycystic kidney disease. Screening for an intracranial **berry aneurysm** in the circle of Willis is critical, as saccular aneurysms occur in eight to twelve percent of ADPKD patients (rising to twenty percent in those with a positive family history of intracranial haemorrhage). Aneurysmal rupture precipitates catastrophic subarachnoid haemorrhage. Magnetic resonance angiography screens high-risk individuals. Additional extrarenal manifestations include polycystic liver disease, mitral valve prolapse, and colonic diverticulosis.
steps.say: Systemic expression of polycystin proteins causes serious extrarenal complications in polycystic kidney disease. Screening for an intracranial berry aneurysm in the circle of Willis is critical, as saccular aneurysms occur in ten percent of patients. Aneurysm rupture causes subarachnoid haemorrhage, requiring magnetic resonance angiography screening in patients with a family history of stroke.

nodes.label: MRA Brain Screening (indicated if family history of stroke/aneurysm)
Detect Saccular Berry Aneurysm -> Endovascular Coiling or Surgical Clipping

steps.tx: Congenital developmental ectasia of collecting ducts produces a distinctive radiological appearance associated with recurrent nephrolithiasis. Diagnosing **medullary sponge kidney** involves cystic dilatation of terminal collecting ducts within the renal pyramids, usually presenting bilaterally. While renal synthetic and glomerular clearance functions remain preserved throughout life, stasis of urine within ectatic medullary ducts predisposes to recurrent calcium oxalate and calcium phosphate calculi, recurrent pyelonephritis, and distal renal tubular acidosis. Excretory intravenous urography or contrast computed tomography classically demonstrates a characteristic bouquet of flowers or paintbrush appearance as contrast fills dilated papillary ducts.
steps.say: Congenital developmental dilatation of medullary collecting ducts causes recurrent kidney stones and infections. Diagnosing medullary sponge kidney involves cystic dilatation of collecting ducts within the pyramids. While glomerular filtration remains normal, urinary stasis causes calcium stones and distal tubular acidosis, with contrast urography showing a classic paintbrush appearance in the papillae.

rows: Cystic dilatation of papillary collecting ducts
Affects inner medulla; renal cortex remains normal
Linear striations of contrast pooling in papillary ducts
Benign course; normal long-term renal survival
Managed with high fluid intake and thiazide diuretics

steps.tx: Defective lysosomal membrane transport leads to widespread intracellular crystal accumulation and infantile proximal tubular failure. Inherited as an autosomal recessive inborn error of metabolism, **cystinosis** results from loss-of-function mutations in the CTNS gene on chromosome seventeen, encoding the lysosomal cystine carrier protein cystinosin. Impaired transport causes intralysosomal cystine crystal precipitation across all organs. Infantile nephropathic cystinosis represents the most common cause of inherited Fanconi syndrome, presenting in infancy with failure to thrive, severe rickets, and photophobia from pathognomonic corneal cystine crystals on slit-lamp biomicroscopy. Oral cysteamine therapy depletes lysosomal cystine.
steps.say: Defective lysosomal transport causes intracellular crystal accumulation and early proximal tubular failure. Inherited as an autosomal recessive metabolic disorder, cystinosis results from mutations in the CTNS gene encoding cystinosin. Cystine crystal accumulation causes severe infantile Fanconi syndrome, growth failure, rickets, and corneal crystal deposition, managed effectively with oral cysteamine therapy.

nodes.label: Defective Cystinosin -> Intralysosomal Cystine Crystal Deposition
Infantile Fanconi Syndrome + Corneal Crystals -> Cysteamine Therapy
